title: AI Impact Self-Assessment
text:
An illustrative self-assessment journey

An illustrative organizational user journey, not a replacement for any framework’s formal assessment process. AI could assist with organizing and reviewing information at each stage; users validate its suggestions and retain control of the conclusions.




01SCOPE


Describe your AI system


Describe the deployed system, its users, and its claimed societal or environmental benefits. A human confirms the scope before proceeding.


System · Users · Intended benefits



↓



02EVIDENCE


Gather supporting evidence


Upload documentation and gather stakeholder input. AI could organize sources and suggest missing information; people verify the record.


Documentation · Stakeholders · Evidence



↓



03ASSESSMENT


Assess its potential impacts


Use framework-based questions on impact, governance, human rights, and social, environmental and economic sustainability. AI could help navigate questions; humans assess the evidence.


Benefits · Harms · Trade-offs



↓



04FINDINGS


Identify risks and evidence gaps


AI could flag unsupported claims, inconsistencies and missing perspectives. Reviewers check those flags and identify unresolved harms and trade-offs.


Uncertainty · Missing evidence · Risks



↓



05OUTPUT


Receive your assessment summary


Review an AI-assisted draft of provisional findings, evidence gaps and next steps. Human approval and possible independent review remain necessary.


Impact snapshot · Priorities · External review

title: AI Impact Self-Assessment
text:
What comes out of it?

Not a certificate that an AI system is “good,” but a clearer starting point for responsible decisions.




OUTPUT 01


Provisional impact profile


A human-reviewed, provisional account of intended benefits, documented effects, possible harms, and open questions.




OUTPUT 02


Evidence & perspective gaps


Potentially AI-flagged gaps and inconsistencies, linked to sources for human verification.




OUTPUT 03


Next-step roadmap


Suggested actions for evidence collection, safeguards, stakeholder engagement, and independent evaluation, confirmed by people.





↗


Why independent perspectives still matter
An organization assessing its own system may overlook harms or overstate benefits. AI-generated suggestions can also be incomplete or misleading. This proposed tool is a preparatory and reflective aid, not a certification or substitute for independent assessment. Human reviewers must check evidence, consider affected stakeholders, and make normative judgments. Rigorous frameworks such as HIIG’s Impact AI Method additionally rely on interviews, qualitative analysis, and external involvement.

section: Towards an Integrated AI Impact Assessment Framework
text:
Towards an Integrated AI Impact Assessment Framework

The five-step self-assessment above illustrates one component of a broader research agenda. I am interested in developing an AI-assisted platform across three complementary pillars, with human oversight and independent perspectives throughout.




POTENTIAL RESEARCH PLATFORM


AI-assisted impact assessment


Framework-informed · Evidence-oriented · Human-in-the-loop




01 · STRUCTURED ASSESSMENT Evidence & stakeholder perspectives Framework-guided review of documentation, interviews, governance, and potential harms (e.g., HIIG’s Impact AI Method). What do we know and how credible is the evidence?


02 · QUANTITATIVE Data & causal evaluation Operational and observational data, descriptive statistics, experiments, and causal designs when appropriate. Did deploying the AI system cause a change in outcomes?


03 · INSTITUTIONAL Use & accountability Human review, institutional adoption, governance, and decisions informed by findings. Does the assessment improve decisions and accountability?

About me





Caio Velasco · Data Scientist · Economics & Public Policy
I am a Brazilian mechanical engineer (UFRJ) with a Master’s in Economics & Public Policy from UCLA (Lemann Foundation scholarship). I have worked internationally in data science, applied econometrics, machine learning, and data engineering, building production data platforms and collaborating with technical and business teams across the US, Europe, and Brazil.
My academic path has also been supported by recognition from UCLA, Lemann Foundation, General Electric Foundation, Yale University, and the Club of Rome.
I am exploring research opportunities at the intersection of AI, societal impact, and evidence-based public policy.



BACKGROUND & LINKS

LinkedIn ↗

Engineering · Empirical Research · Applied AI




HIIG’s interest in future organizational self-assessment is a welcome coincidence with my interest in AI-assisted tools and applied AI governance.
This page presents my own exploratory user journey, developed in connection with an application to the Impact AI Fellowship 2027. It is not a functioning AI assessment system, has not been empirically validated, and has not been commissioned or endorsed by HIIG. No real AI system has been assessed here.
